title: FFIEC adds agent-harness third-party risk addendum by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council publishes a focused addendum to the FFIEC Outsourcing Technology Services and Architecture, Infrastructure, and Operations booklets that explicitly extends bank third-party-risk supervision to agent-harness loaders and MCP-server channels, jointly signed by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, the FDIC, the NCUA, and the CFPB, with the addendum citing CVE-2026-46127 and the Mandiant Fortune 500 financial-services active-exploitation finding as the precipitating risk event. Tuesday's GitHub Security Lab advisory on CVE-2026-46127 in OpenAI's Codex CLI carried two operational features the prudential-supervisor cohort treats as activating triggers for a fresh booklet addendum rather than a footnote update inside an existing examination cycle: first, CISA's same-window placement of the CVE on the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog inside the Mandiant incident-response engagement at a Fortune 500 financial-services customer establishes a documented in-the-wild loss exposure at a supervised entity rather than a hypothetical risk surface, and second, NIST NVD's same-day reclassification under the new agent-loader subcategory lifts the Trail of Bits agent-harness CVE taxonomy to twelve cataloged instances which the booklet's existing third-party-risk taxonomy does not enumerate as a covered class. The structural force is that once a Fortune 500 supervised entity has a confirmed agent-harness in-the-wild exploitation event on the CISA KEV catalog with the underlying CVE class crossing into double-digit cataloged instances and NIST formally promoting a dedicated subcategory, the interagency cohort's standing examination workflow no longer has a defensible reading that agent-harness third-party-risk falls under the generic outsourced-technology-service framing — the booklet addendum becomes the cheapest compliance pathway for both the supervised entities and the supervisor staff conducting the next examination cycle. The most likely landing is the FFIEC publishing the addendum in a 60-90 day federal-register comment window opening inside the back half of June with a final version effective inside Q3 2026, the addendum naming the OWASP LLM Top 10 v2 prompt-injection and MCP-channel categories plus the Trail of Bits agent-harness CVE taxonomy as the canonical reference taxonomies for the agent-loader risk class, the FS-ISAC publishing a sector-coordinated playbook citing the addendum inside the same window, and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York including agent-harness third-party-risk in the next round of supervisory letters to the largest bank holding companies. Bear case is the interagency cohort defers a standalone booklet addendum and instead folds agent-harness third-party-risk into the next annual update to the existing Outsourcing booklet inside Q4 2026 with the addendum draft circulating as an informal interagency examination expectation through Q3; absent that fold-in, Q3 2026 lands the FFIEC addendum as the first prudential-regulator artifact that names agent-harness loaders as a supervised third-party-risk class.

reasoning.because: CVE-2026-46127 hits CISA KEV with Mandiant exploitation at a Fortune 500 bank customer.
reasoning.given: NIST NVD opens agent-loader subcategory; Trail of Bits taxonomy crosses twelve cataloged CVEs.
reasoning.so_that: FFIEC publishes booklet addendum naming agent-harness loaders and MCP channels as supervised risk class.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; OCC, FRB, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB jointly sign; FS-ISAC playbook follows.
reasoning.plain_language: Bank regulators will write a new rule so banks must check the AI tools their vendors use, because hackers just broke in.

summary: CVE-2026-46127 in OpenAI Codex CLI hits CISA KEV with Mandiant confirming exploitation at a Fortune 500 bank customer, and NIST NVD opens a dedicated agent-loader subcategory. By Q3 2026 the FFIEC publishes a jointly signed addendum bringing agent-harness loaders under bank vendor-risk rules.
